sentences.text: This gate reads all six attributes. It acts on 96 of 345 training cases, 7 of which are actually 'yes'; for the typical case it acts on (no attribute at its first value: a1 = 2, a2 = 3, a3 = 2, a4 = 2, a5 = 4, a6 = 2), it takes the predicted probability of 'yes' from above 99% without it to below 1% with it.

How much a3 = 2 instead of 1 moves the prediction depends on a6 and a5: for the typical case, it takes the predicted probability of 'yes' from below 1% to above 99% when a6 = 2 and to about 72% when a5 = 3, but leaves it below 1% when a6 = 1 or a5 = 1.
Through it, moving a1, a3, a5 or a6 away from its first value lowers the probability and a2 = 1, a4 = 1 or a4 = 3 instead of 2 raises it, all below 1% for the typical case it acts on.

This ramp adds up all six attributes with fixed weights. Through it, moving a6, a3, a1 or a5 away from its first value raises the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes', and giving a2 or a4 its first value lowers it, as do a2 = 2 instead of 3 and a4 = 3 instead of 2, though it stays below 1%.
Across the whole model, a2 = 2 instead of 3 lowers it, while the typical case stays below 1%.

lead.text: For the typical case (the most common value of each attribute: a1 = 1, a2 = 3, a3 = 1, a4 = 2, a5 = 1, a6 = 1) the model gives a predicted probability of 'yes' below 1%; it adds up two parts: a gate that pulls 'yes' down for the 96 training cases it acts on, and a ramp that falls as more attributes take their first value.

Through it, moving a1, a3, a5 or a6 away from its first value lowers the probability and a2 = 1, a4 = 1 or a4 = 3 instead of 2 raises it, all below 1% for the typical case it acts on.

parts.name: two_indicator_peak
parts.original_hypothesis: Output = sigmoid(Ramp - 7.61 * Gate - 0.93): an additive composition in logit space. The descending ramp makes counts >= 3 negative; the at-most-one gate overrides the ramp's high values at counts 0-1. The logit therefore peaks at exactly two first-value indicators. Inputs a1:3, a2:2, a3:2, a5:2, a5:4 have no enabled connections and are zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, full sample): AUC 1.0 - every count-2 row outranks every other row - but the margin is thin (min positive logit -3.52 vs max negative -3.75), and the threshold is miscalibrated: only 86/113 count-2 rows exceed 0.5 (accuracy 0.922); the misses are pairs involving a3/a6/a5/a1 where the ramp's heavier weights push the logit below zero. No count != 2 row is predicted positive.

parts.name: few_indicators_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: An at-most-one-of-six detector (lower edge of the peak). ReLU unit 773 = relu(-3.54 a1:1 - 4.17 a2:1 - 4.41 a3:1 - 2.27 a4:1 - 3.72 a5:1 - 4.16 a6:1 + 1.52 a4:2 - 0.07 a1:2 + 0.21 a5:3 - 4.47) on z-scored inputs. In indicator terms its pre-activation is about +12 to +16 when no attribute takes its first value, and each first-value indicator subtracts 4.9-8.8. Evidence (train, n=345, full sample): active on 19/19 count-0 and 70/70 count-1 rows, on only 7/113 count-2 rows (pairs a1&a4 and one a1&a6, activation <= 0.52) and on 0/143 rows with count >= 3. Its -7.61 readout drives low-count logits to between -99 and -12. Alone it ranks the classes with AUC 0.67.

parts.name: descending_count_ramp
parts.original_hypothesis: A linear ramp that falls with the number of first-value indicators (upper edge of the peak). The ten direct input->output edges give each attribute's first value a contribution 7-12 lower than its other values (a1 -10.2, a2 -8.2 vs a2=2 / -11.9 vs a2=3, a3 -12.1, a4 -7.6/-6.9, a5 -10.0, a6 -12.2). Evidence (train, full sample): ramp + output bias lies in [21.3, 25.7] at count 0, [8.6, 18.2] at count 1, [-3.5, 7.9] at count 2 and below -3.7 for every count >= 3 row, so it crosses zero between two and three indicators. Weights are not uniform: a3 and a6 (binary attributes) carry the largest drops, so count-2 rows involving a3 or a6 sit closest to zero. Alone it ranks poorly (AUC 0.62) because counts 0-1 score highest.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording
